title: Probe and needle on the patient
view: Right neck from above, patient supine, head turned to the left: head at the top, the patient's right (shoulder) on the image left, as the anatomy plate and the interscalene plate.
teachingPoint: Probe transverse in the supraclavicular fossa, just above the clavicle and parallel to it, handle tilted toward the head so the beam aims caudally; needle in-plane from the lateral end.
claims: Right neck from above, head turned left; lateral on the image left, the same way round as the anatomy plate (camera reused from the approved interscalene plate).

Linear probe transverse in the supraclavicular fossa, just above and parallel to the clavicle (record subtitle and step 4; placement over the middle of the clavicle, lateral to the SCM's clavicular head, is standard anatomy added here).
Handle rising toward the head: the caudal aim (record subtitle).
Needle entering just beyond the probe's lateral end, in line: in-plane from lateral to medial (record, step 6).
Labels: Block needle, Linear probe, Clavicle.

geometry.why: probe face sits on the skin above the bone, not on it
probe sits in the supraclavicular hollow
probe's medial end reaches the SCM's lateral border, no further
handle rises toward the head: caudal aim
needle enters at the lateral end
needle path clear of the external jugular
head turned away; the ear is up and lateral
